snp3.2:2.1: Nāmuci is an epithet for Māra.
snp3.2:11.2: The highest equanimity that can be attained through jhāna.
snp3.2:16.1: Muñja grass was the ancient Indian equivalent of a white flag: a warrior expecting he might have to surrender would carry it into battle, and lie down with it in his mouth if he did surrender. The Buddha’s rhetorical question indicates he is not that kind of warrior—he would rather die than surrender.
snp3.2:16.4: This line is repeated at Thag 2:37.
snp3.2:25.5: vv. 425–449. See also: MN 70; SN 4; AN 2:5; AN 5:53.
